_comment: Registration for the age verb of scripts/lane-file.py (issue #1696).
WHY AN ADVISORY NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): its verdict is read by
an owner and by a planning session that will not re-derive the lane file's
age. A blind version prints the same 'fresh' line over a list nobody has
read in a year, and the plan table built from that list still looks complete.
THE DATE IS PINNED. Every case is run with --today 2026-03-02, so the
verdict does not move with the calendar. 2025-12-31 is 61 days before it
and 2026-01-01 is exactly 60; the default threshold is 60.
TWO BAD CASES, because the advisory has two ways to be owed: a review that
is old, and a list whose review nobody can date. The second must read
limits: Covers the AGE VERDICT for a readable lane file against the default 60-day threshold, at a pinned date. It does not cover the absent state, the unusable-file states (unreadable, directory, dangling symlink, unsearchable parent, future or impossible date, disagreeing dates), the stamp verb, or root resolution - those are pinned by tests/test_lane_file.py. It says nothing about whether the lane list is COMPLETE: a freshly stamped list can still omit a lane.

cases.name: bad-one-day-past
cases.why: Reviewed 2025-12-31, 61 days before the pinned date - ONE day over the threshold, the #1696 acceptance case. If it scores GOOD the advisory cannot see an old review.

cases.name: bad-no-review-date
cases.why: A lane file with no Reviewed: line. Its age is unknown; if it scores GOOD an undated list is being read as a fresh one.

cases.name: good-at-threshold
cases.why: Reviewed 2026-01-01, exactly 60 days before the pinned date. Separates a working advisory from one wedged at 'stale', and pins the boundary as inclusive.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: the plausible weaker check - the project has a lane file - with the review date never read. 'It keeps a lane list' mistaken for 'the list was reviewed recently'. It reports fresh on cases/bad-one-day-past and on cases/bad-no-review-date.
